grades.reason: Discusses mmap versus pread/pwrite in the POSIX file API. It says nothing about diagnosing page faults or telling permission faults from missing mappings.
Covers which faulting address is reported in mtval/stval/htval for guest-page faults that straddle page boundaries. It gives no way to tell a permission fault from a missing mapping.

grades.quote: PTE_V indicates whether the PTE is present: if it is not set, a reference to the page causes a page fault (i.e., is not allowed).
grades.reason: Explains the RISC-V PTE flag bits. A page fault with PTE_V clear means no valid mapping, while the R/W/X/U bits give permission-based denial. This tells you what to check in the PTE, but it never names the fault cause codes or gives a step-by-step diagnosis.

grades.quote: When SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1 in Figure 67) will fault.
grades.reason: Describes how the MXR and SUM bits in sstatus change access permissions and can cause permission faults, for example S-mode touching U pages with SUM=0. This helps when investigating a permission fault, but it does not explain how to tell it from a missing mapping.
